2027-03-04.title: Fourth Thursday of the Great Fast
2027-03-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-03-04.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). In the Latin calendar, St Casimir is commemorated today.
2027-03-04.verse: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.
theo: Lot had chosen the well-watered plain and moved his tent toward Sodom. Now the kings of the region go to war, Sodom is plundered, and “they also took Lot, the son of Abram's brother, who lived in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.” Abram could have said: he chose it; let him live with it. Instead, “When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred eighteen of them, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.” He fights by night, routs the raiders, and “brought back his nephew Lot with his goods, and the women and the people.” This is the love that goes after the one who walked away. Many of us have a Lot in the family: a son who chose another road, a sister who moved far from the faith, a relative who is now caught in debt or drink. The Great Fast asks us not to say “he chose it” but to go after them with prayer, patience and practical help. In the verses that follow, Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, comes out to meet Abram with bread and wine (Genesis 14:18). The Letter to the Hebrews sees in him a figure of Christ the eternal priest, and the Church sees in his offering a figure of the bread and wine of the Holy Qurbana.

After the victory at Ai, Joshua does something unexpected: he stops to worship. He builds on Mount Ebal “an altar of unhewn stones, on which no iron tool has been used”, offers sacrifices, writes the law on stones, and then reads it aloud. “There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, and the women, and the little ones, and the aliens who resided among them.” Word and altar, everyone gathered, no one left out: this is the shape of every Holy Qurbana. First the word of God is proclaimed to the whole assembly, then the offering is made on the altar. And notice who is there: women, little ones and strangers. Children belong at the Holy Qurbana, not only when they behave; and the readings belong to them too, if parents take a minute on the way home to ask what they heard.

Paul asks the question many Christians have asked carelessly: “has God rejected his people? By no means!” He answers as an Israelite himself: “God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.” When Elijah complained that he alone was left, God answered: “I have kept for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal.” “So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace.” The Second Vatican Council, drawing on these chapters, taught that the Jews remain most dear to God for the sake of their fathers, for God does not take back his gifts or his call (Nostra Aetate 4). Elijah's complaint is also our temptation: to think we are the only faithful ones left. God always has his seven thousand. In the Gospel the festival of Booths is near, the great autumn feast when Israel lived in shelters to remember the desert. Jesus' relatives urge him to go up and make a name: “no one who wants to be widely known acts in secret.” John adds sadly: “(For not even his brothers believed in him.)” Jesus answers: “My time has not yet come”, and later goes up “not publicly but as it were in secret.” The crowds argue about him, but no one speaks openly “for fear of the Jews”, which in John means fear of certain authorities, since the crowds themselves were Jews. Jesus does not follow the timetable of publicity. He waits for the Father's hour, and in this fast he teaches us to do our good works in secret too.
outline: Ask: who is the Lot in my family, and have I gone after him?
Abram rescues the one who chose another road.
Joshua reads the law to all, women, children and strangers.
A remnant chosen by grace, and Jesus who waits for the Father's hour.
“God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.”
live: Phone, visit or write to one relative or friend who has drifted away, without lecturing; simply show that you care.
Take the children to the Holy Qurbana this week and on the way home ask each one what they heard in the readings.
2027-03-04.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you went after us when we had chosen the road to Sodom, and you brought us back. Give us the heart of Abram for those who have strayed, the faith of Joshua who gathered all the people around the word and the altar, and the patience to wait for the Father's hour. Keep us from thinking we alone are faithful, and bless the people of the first covenant, whom you have never rejected. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana, as at Mount Ebal, the whole people gathers: the word is read to all, and the offering is made on the altar. Melchizedek's bread and wine find their fulfilment in the Body and Blood of Christ, the eternal priest.

quick: Abram went after Lot, who had chosen Sodom, and brought him home.
Joshua built an altar and read the whole law to all the people, including women, children and strangers.
God has not rejected his people; Jesus waits for the Father's hour and goes up in secret.
2027-03-04.action: Contact one relative or friend who has drifted away, simply to show you care.
2027-03-04.question: Do I go after those who have strayed, or do I say: they chose it?

family.explain: Abram's nephew Lot had gone to live in a bad city. One day enemies captured him and took him away. Abram did not say: it is his own fault. He gathered his men, chased the enemies all through the night, and brought Lot home safely. God wants us to help people even when they have made wrong choices.
family.intention: We pray for members of our family who have drifted away from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we know who needs us to go after them with kindness this week?”

illus: A mother in Kanjirappally had a son who left home angry at twenty and stopped coming to church. Every Thursday for nine years she went to the parish adoration chapel and prayed for him, and every month she sent him a short message, never a sermon, only news of home and “we love you.” He told his own children later that the messages were the thread that held him. When he finally walked into the church on a Good Friday, she was in her usual place, and she simply moved over to make room.

pm.open: Lord, you go after the lost and gather your people around your word and your altar. Gather us now. Amen.
share: When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he went in pursuit (Genesis 14:14). Whom is God asking me to go after?
Joshua read every word before all the assembly, women and children and strangers (Joshua 8:35). Do I make room for others at the word and the altar?
There is a remnant, chosen by grace (Romans 11:5). Do I think I am the only faithful one left?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us into your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may go after every lost sheep.
For families with members who have drifted from the faith.
For the Jewish people, beloved of God for the sake of their fathers.
For children, that they may come to love the word of God and the Holy Qurbana.
For our group, that we may do our good works in secret, for the Father alone.
pm.close: Father, you never reject your people and you send your Son after those who stray. Make us faithful to your word and your altar, and bring back all who have wandered. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Lot chose to live near Sodom, and when enemies captured him, Abram did not say: it is his own fault. He took his men, went in pursuit as far as Dan, and brought Lot home (Genesis 14:14–16). Is there a Lot in our family? Let us go after him with prayer and with love.

After the battle, Joshua builds an altar and reads every word of the law before all the people, the women, the little ones and the strangers (Joshua 8:35). This is the shape of our Holy Qurbana: the word read to all, and the offering on the altar. Let us bring our children, and help them hear.
Paul says: God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew (Romans 11:2). God keeps a remnant chosen by grace. We honour the Jewish people, and we never think that we alone are faithful.

Jesus' relatives want him to go and make a name for himself. He says: my time has not yet come, and he goes up to the feast in secret (John 7:6, 10). In this fast, let us also do our good in secret, and trust the Father's time. Amen.
kids: Children, Abram's nephew got into big trouble because of his own choices, but Abram still went to rescue him! Can you be kind today to someone who has been naughty or unkind? That is what Jesus does for us.

intro: Theme: “God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.”
Abram goes after Lot, Joshua gathers all the people around the word and the altar, God keeps a remnant by grace, and Jesus waits for the Father's hour.

sub: Abram did not say: it is his fault.
Love that goes after the one who strayed.
q: When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred eighteen of them, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
“Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
points.apply: Contact one person who has drifted away, simply to show that you care.

q: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, and the women, and the little ones, and the aliens who resided among them.
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: After this week's Holy Qurbana, ask each child at home what they heard in the readings.

sub: God has not rejected his people.
Jesus waits for the Father's hour.
q: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
So too at the present time there is a remnant, chosen by grace.
points.apply: Do one good work this week in secret, and do not mention it to anyone.

concl: God goes after the lost, gathers all his people, and never takes back his call.
Let us go after those who have strayed, make room for everyone at the word and the altar, and trust the Father's hour.
2027-03-04.resolve: This week, reach out to one person who has drifted away, and bring the children to the word and the altar.
